outcome: success of breastfeeding in the delivery room
cohort: 2,008 biological mothers in Hungary who had raised their at least 5-year-old child(ren) at home
finding: Obstetric interventions were associated with a higher likelihood of further interventions and negatively impacted early breastfeeding success.
mod_finding: Mothers who gave birth naturally and used oxytocin had lower breastfeeding success in the delivery room, while newborns born naturally had higher rates of breastfeeding in the delivery room and less formula feeding in the hospital.
